## Course setup

- Parallel to the first-year **programming** course
- This course: biological questions → quantitative tools
- 14 weeks; each week has `slides.qmd`, `notebook.qmd`, `assignment.qmd` under `weeks/week-XX/`
- **[AI policy](ai-policy.qmd)** — generative AI allowed for learning; graded work must be yours + disclosed if AI helped

### Lecture slot

- **Thursdays, 08:15–10:00**
- First session: **17 Sep 2026**
- Then weekly through **17 Dec 2026** (14 meetings; no skipped weeks in this plan — adjust if the faculty calendar cancels a Thursday)

### Biological arc

```text
Eco  →  Evo (deterministic → random)  →  Microbiome (ecology with randomness)
```

| Block | Weeks | Biology | Quantitative focus | Checkpoint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hook** | 1 | Human adaptation: Bajau diving → Tibetan altitude | Why cool biology needs many tools | — |
| **Ecology** | 2–4 | Populations & interactions | Deterministic simulation (function → vector → loop) | **A · Week 4** |
| **Evolution (deterministic)** | 5–7 | Allele-frequency change, selection | Recurrence equations; same coding engine | **B · Week 7** |
| **Evolution (random)** | 8–10 | Establishment → evolutionary rescue | Stochastic fates; lab-tested rescue theory | **C · Week 10** |
| **Microbiome** | 11–13 | Complex community datasets | Load → wrangle → visualize high-dimensional tables | **D · Week 13** |
| **Synthesis** | 14 | Pull the arc together | Reflect / optional mini-extension | Light wrap (not the only graded talk) |

**Punchline of the semester:** deterministic ecological dynamics → evolutionary change (smooth, then establishment/rescue under randomness) → return to ecology as **complex data** you must load and visualize carefully.

### Assessment rhythm (presentations throughout)

Rather than one big end-of-term talk, grade **four block checkpoints**. After every content block (~3 weeks) there is a **bigger practical** and a **short presentation session**.

| Checkpoint | When | Theme | Practical (graded product) | Presentation (short) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | Week **4** · **8 Oct 2026** | Ecology | Own mini-model + plot vs real series (Isle Royale / Gause) | ~3–4 min: story → model → one plot → one limitation |
| **B** | Week **7** · **29 Oct 2026** | Evolution (deterministic) | Selection regime comparison (\(p_t\) trajectories) | Same format; emphasize recurrence / equilibria |
| **C** | Week **10** · **19 Nov 2026** | Evolutionary rescue | Rescue / establishment simulation + link to a lab result | When does a declining population adapt in time? |
| **D** | Week **13** · **10 Dec 2026** | Microbiome data viz | Load + visualize a real community table; one clear figure story | What the plot shows — and what it does **not** |
| Wrap | Week **14** · **17 Dec 2026** | Synthesis | Optional polish / peer feedback / ILIAS cleanup | Not a fifth high-stakes talk — connect A–D |

**Suggested grading (draft — tune with collabs):** roughly equal weight on checkpoints A–D (practical + presentation each); weekly notebooks more formative. Exact % live in ILIAS.

**Presentation norms (all checkpoints):**

- Pairs or small groups preferred
- Hard cap (~3–5 min) + 1–2 questions
- Required beats: (1) biological question, (2) what you computed, (3) one figure, (4) strongest assumption / next step
- Grade for clarity + biological sense + honest limitations — not for fancy graphics

### Programming bridge

| Concept | Where |
|---|---|
| Function | next-state updates |
| Vector | ecological / genetic time series |
| Loop | many steps / generations |
| Plot | interpretation; microbiome multi-panel viz |
| Matrix / tables | establishment/rescue replicates; abundance tables |

## Week 1 — Hook: two extremes of human adaptation

**When:** Thu 17 Sep 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Biology:** Bajau diving (Andika) → Tibetan high altitude (EPAS1)  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-01/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-01/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-01/assignment.qmd)

- Personal story + photo hook (Andika / Bajau)
- Physiology → genetics: PDE10A, BDKRB2 from **modern-human** variation; possible Denisovan-related **FAM178B**
- Second extreme: Tibetan highland adaptation; **EPAS1** as cleaner Denisovan teaching case (Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014)
- **Close:** message-board glossary — *population*, *gene*, *generation*, *selection* (+ optional lab stickers)
- Papers: Ilardo et al. 2018 *Cell*; Ilardo et al. 2021 *Front. Physiol.*; Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014 *Nature*
- Foreshadow: later blocks end with a **short graded presentation**, not only a final exam talk

## Ecology (Weeks 2–4) → Checkpoint A

Engine: biological rule → discrete update → `next_state()` → vectors → loop → plot

### Week 2 — From cool dynamics to code
**When:** Thu 24 Sep 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-02/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-02/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-02/assignment.qmd)

- **Bio opener integrated:** *Paramecium* alone vs with *Didinium* (Gause / Veilleux tradition)
- Data in `weeks/week-02/data/`
- Discrete LV → function / vector / loop; qualitative link back to the contrast

### Week 3 — Richer ecological models
**When:** Thu 1 Oct 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-03/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-03/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-03/assignment.qmd)

- **Bio opener:** Gause (1934) Fig. 22 — *P. caudatum* vs *P. aurelia* alone vs mixture (`weeks/week-03/data/`)
- Carrying capacity \(K\); two-species competition; parameter play

### Week 4 — Ecological data, your own model, **Checkpoint A**
**When:** Thu 8 Oct 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-04/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-04/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-04/assignment.qmd)

- **Bio opener:** Isle Royale moose–wolf (McLaren & Peterson 1994); optional Huffaker / lynx (`weeks/week-04/data/`)
- Qualitative model–data comparison; model zoo; build your own simulation
- **Session shape:** guided work → **bigger practical** → **presentation session** (Checkpoint A)
- Graded: mini-model write-up + short talk (see Assessment rhythm)

## Evolution — deterministic (Weeks 5–7) → Checkpoint B

Same engine; object = **allele frequency** \(p_t\).

### Week 5 — Allele frequencies as time series
**When:** Thu 15 Oct 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-05/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-05/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-05/assignment.qmd)

- Vectors for \(p_t\); selection recurrence \(p_{t+1}=f(p_t)\); one-generation function

### Week 6 — Selection regimes
**When:** Thu 22 Oct 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-06/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-06/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-06/assignment.qmd)

- Many generations; compare regimes; equilibria / trajectories

### Week 7 — Limits of deterministic evolution + **Checkpoint B**
**When:** Thu 29 Oct 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-07/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-07/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-07/assignment.qmd)

- Smooth \(p_t\) as average behavior; motivate randomness
- **Checkpoint B:** compare ≥2 selection regimes; present one figure + when the deterministic story is not enough
- Bridge forward: a beneficial allele that starts as a **single copy** may never establish — even if selection is “strong” on average

## Evolution — random (Weeks 8–10) → Checkpoint C

**Pedagogical arc:** deterministic selection → **establishment probabilities** → **evolutionary rescue** (a pop-gen theory extensively tested in the lab).

Same coding engine as before; new object = **fate of rare beneficial types** (survive vs lost), then **population persistence** under stress.

### Week 8 — From deterministic selection to establishment
**When:** Thu 5 Nov 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-08/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-08/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-08/assignment.qmd)

- Recap Weeks 5–7: smooth \(p_t\) when many copies already segregate
- Punchline: a **new** beneficial mutant starts at count 1 — randomness decides early fate
- Introduce **establishment probability** (intuition: branching-process / many failed starts)
- Simulation: many independent introductions; fraction that “take off”
- Still optional: classic \(u \approx 2s\) as a target to compare against (haploid / weak selection)

### Week 9 — Establishment probabilities in code
**When:** Thu 12 Nov 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-09/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-09/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-09/assignment.qmd)

- Build / refine an establishment simulator (loop over replicates; store outcomes in a vector/matrix)
- Explore how establishment depends on selection coefficient \(s\), population size, and starting copy number
- Compare simulation estimates to a simple analytic benchmark
- Biological reading: why “supply of mutations × establishment” matters for adaptation from new mutation

### Week 10 — Evolutionary rescue + **Checkpoint C**
**When:** Thu 19 Nov 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-10/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-10/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-10/assignment.qmd)

- **Biology:** population declining under environmental stress; adaptation must establish **before extinction**
- Minimal rescue model: demography (decline) + rare beneficial / resistant types + establishment
- **Lab link:** evolutionary rescue is one of the pop-gen ideas most thoroughly tested in microbes (yeast, bacteria) under controlled stress
  - Classic theory: Gomulkiewicz & Holt; Orr & Unckless, etc.
  - Experiments: e.g. Bell & Gonzalez and related microbial rescue / persistence assays (cite precisely in slides)
- **Checkpoint C:** simulate a rescue scenario; present (1) question, (2) establishment vs extinction outcomes, (3) one figure, (4) what a lab experiment would measure

## Microbiome — loading & visualizing complex data (Weeks 11–13) → Checkpoint D

Return to **ecology**, but now the bottleneck is practical: **high-dimensional, messy tables**.

**Pedagogical arc:** load complex data → exploratory visualization → a graded visual story (Checkpoint D).

Easy to fill 2–3 weeks: file formats, abundance matrices, metadata joins, relative vs absolute abundances, composition plots, heatmaps, faceting by host/site/time, and honest captions.

### Week 11 — Loading complex microbiome data
**When:** Thu 26 Nov 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-11/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-11/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-11/assignment.qmd)

- What a microbiome dataset looks like: samples × taxa (+ taxonomy) + **metadata**
- Read CSV/TSV (and note BIOM / QIIME-style exports as “exists in the wild”)
- Tidy principles: long vs wide abundance tables; join metadata safely
- Sanity checks: library size, missing values, sparse zeros, sample IDs that don’t match
- First numerical summaries only (totals per sample) — **plots next week**

### Week 12 — Visualizing community data
**When:** Thu 3 Dec 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-12/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-12/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-12/assignment.qmd)

- Grammar of graphics for many taxa: choose **aggregations** (top taxa, phylum rolls)
- Core plot types: stacked composition, heatmap, facet by group/time, simple diversity bars if useful
- Visual pitfalls: ordering, colour overload, compositional constraints, log scales
- Programming bridge: reuse vectors/matrices; build reusable plotting functions

### Week 13 — A visual story + **Checkpoint D**
**When:** Thu 10 Dec 2026, 08:15–10:00  
**Materials:** [slides](../weeks/week-13/slides.qmd) · [notebook](../weeks/week-13/notebook.qmd) · [assignment](../weeks/week-13/assignment.qmd)

- Compare groups or time points with a **small figure set** (not a fishing expedition)
- Optional light summaries (richness / simple beta viz) only insofar as they support the story
- **Checkpoint D:** load → clean → visualize → present one clear claim with limits
- Emphasis: communication quality of figures > exotic methods
